key_insight: Early reasoning steps show larger activation fluctuations, which standard calibration may miss. Accounting for these early states could help preserve reasoning quality when models run at low precision.
problem_solved: Large reasoning models generate long reasoning traces that increase inference costs, but aggressive quantization can degrade reasoning performance.
method: Analyze activation fluctuations during the first decoding steps of reasoning.
Motivate calibration that captures early reasoning states rather than omitting them.
The title indicates enhanced outlier mitigation and adaptive clustering; implementation details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: This work targets more efficient reasoning-model inference without sacrificing reasoning quality. It highlights early-step calibration coverage as a practical consideration, although the supplied excerpt provides no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Activation-over-time plot highlighting fluctuations in the first reasoning steps.
Calibration coverage diagram contrasting omitted versus included early decoding states.
Conceptual schematic of outlier mitigation and adaptive clustering.
Inference cost versus reasoning quality trade-off graphic, labeled conceptual.
paper_title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
paper_authors: Xingyu Liu, Xiangyang Yin, Tianhua Xia, Haiyu Wang, Sai Qian Zhang
